title: Model Catalog: Verified Profiles -- GTM & PM Brief
objective: Align GTM, PM, and SE on how we will present 'Verified Profiles' for open models in the Redwood catalog so engineering buyers can make defensible model choices quickly.
audience: GTM leads, product marketing, product managers (model catalog), sales engineers, solutions engineering
context: We will add standardized, short profiles to open models that combine machine measurements, Redwood verification notes, and operational playbooks. Goal is to reduce friction in model selection for production SLOs.
primary_goals: Help engineers pick models that meet latency, cost, and quality targets without lengthy internal experiments
Increase conversion from catalog browsing to first API call and Dedicated trial activation
Differentiate Redwood by pairing reproducible measurements with production playbooks and operational guidance
messaging_pillars: Predictable economics: per-model cost guidance, recommended quantization and batching, real latency ranges
Production-ready quality: concise, comparable eval highlights and known failure modes
Integration-ready: clear notes on supported runtime features and compatibilities
Human verification: short applied-ML sign-off explaining where the model shines
Operational resilience: suggested fallbacks and routing recommendations
profile_minimal_fields: latency_p50 at seq lengths [128, 512, 2048] on Redwood hosted GPU
competitive_notes: OpenAI: strong brand and polished DX; they don't publish granular per-model runtime cost tradeoffs for open models. Our advantage: transparent unit economics and reproducible harnesses for open models.
Hugging Face: excellent discovery and community content but inconsistent metrics and few production playbooks. We provide curated, machine-executed metrics plus human guidance for ops.
Self-hosted runtimes (MLC/Ollama/etc): great for full control but require customers to benchmark and tune. Redwood supplies pre-computed knobs, fallback policies, and hosted paths for fast POCs.

Cloud managed model endpoints: enterprise integrations and SLAs. Redwood differentiates by offering a unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private plus verified model profiles that guide deployment choices.
sales_objections_and_rebuttals: "Why not just pick the largest model?": Larger models often increase latency and cost without commensurate gains for many tasks. Verified Profiles highlight where smaller models or quantized variants hit the sweet spot.
"How reliable are your metrics?": All published numbers link to the harness, seed config, and infra used. We run reproducible tests and surface known dataset biases and caveats.
"Are these profiles locked to Redwood?": No. Profiles are recommendations and exportable. Customers can reproduce harnesses in a VPC or use our Hosted/Dedicated options.

"Do these imply performance guarantees?": Profiles state measured ranges on our infra and include a clear disclaimer about differences on customer data and infra; we avoid promising SLAs solely based on a profile.
elevator_copy: Pick models with confidence. Redwood Verified Profiles combine reproducible latency, cost, and quality signals with production playbooks so engineering teams can choose models that meet real SLOs instead of guessing.
micro_headlines_for_tests: Choose models by your SLOs: latency, cost, quality
Verified profiles for open models  benchmarks, runtime recommendations, playbooks

one_paragraph_marketing: Redwood Verified Profiles make model selection repeatable and fast. Each profile bundles reproducible benchmark results, recommended runtime and quantization settings, and short operational guidance from our Applied ML team. The catalog surfaces models by the tradeoffs that matter  token economics, latency at typical sequence lengths, and task-specific quality  so teams can find the right model for chat, retrieval augmentation, code generation, or embeddings without long engineering experiments.

Per-model runtime recommendations and cost estimates

outreach_subject_lines: See which model actually meets your SLOs  instantly
Verified profiles: pick models without the guesswork

faq_snippets: Q: What does "verified" mean? A: We run a standardized evaluation harness on representative infra and combine automated metrics with a human review that highlights operational caveats.
Q: Can I reproduce these results? A: Yes. Each profile links to the harness, seed configs, and Docker/runtime notes so you can replicate locally or in your VPC.
Q: Are these recommendations final? A: No. Profiles are starting points and include validation prompts and known failure modes to try against your data.
launch_tactical_plan_90_days: Weeks 0-2: Cross-functional kickoff (PM, Applied ML, Product Marketing, Sales Eng); scope 8 seed profiles across high-value categories (chat, embeddings, code, reranking).
Weeks 2-4: Publish catalog pages, downloadable harnesses, and short demo videos. Add "reproduce" buttons linking to artifact bundles.
Weeks 4-8: A/B test hero copy and CTA; instrument metrics for model-to-first-call and conversion lift; enable sample queries in the console using recommended prompt templates.
Weeks 8-12: Collect customer feedback, iterate profiles, expand nightly harness runs for top models, and publish known-issues and FAQ updates.

sample_profile_sketch: Description: Low-latency instruction-tuned model for chat and short completions.
Use cases: internal help desk bot, short doc summarization, lightweight code assistance
Recommended quant: int8 (approx 2.1x cost reduction vs fp16)
Strengths: fast on short prompts, consistent instruction-following, compact memory footprint
Failures: multi-hop factual reasoning, degraded coherence beyond 3k tokens
Fallback: redwood-alpaca-13b (automated routing: scale up + increase timeout)
notes_to_sales: Lead with the one-liner and two quick bullets on how Verified Profiles speeds POC and reduces wasteful engineering time.
Use the FAQ snippets during discovery to defuse concerns about metric trust and reproducibility.
